title: Elementary etale devissage of a finite type module
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, where $s=f(x)$, $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and $\mathcal F_s$ is its pullback to this fibre. Put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, where support is the locus of nonzero stalks and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-dimension]. There are etale pointed neighbourhoods $g:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ and $e:(S',s')\to(S,s)$ inducing isomorphisms of residue fields at the distinguished points, with $f g=e f'$ for a map $f':X'\to S'$, a closed immersion $i:Z'\to X'$ of finite presentation, a finite map $\pi:Z'\to Y'$ over $S'$, and a finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $Z'$. All four schemes $X',Z',Y',S'$ are affine, $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$, and $h:Y'\to S'$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres. Here geometrically integral means integral after every extension of the residue field of a fibre. There is a point $z'\in Z'$ with $i(z')=x'$, and if $y'=\pi(z')$ then $h(y')=s'$, $\pi^{-1}(y')=\{z'\}$, and $\kappa(y')/\kappa(s')$ is purely transcendental. Smooth has the meaning of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and etale that of [def-weil-etale-morphism]; finite and closed immersion have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: Apply the affine fibre-support model to $f,\mathcal F,x$. Obtain $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow S$, $p:U\to V$, $j:Z\hookrightarrow U$, $\mathcal H$ and $z$ with $j_*\mathcal H\cong u^*\mathcal F$ and $\dim_z Z_s=n$. All three schemes $U,V,Z$ are affine and $pj$ is finite type. The inclusions preserve residue fields.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, affine reduction and the supporting-scheme construction.

proof.text: Apply the finite-over-smooth local structure theorem to $pj:Z\to V$ at $z$. It gives affine $W,Y,S_1$, elementary etale $b:(W,w)\to(Z,z)$ and $a:(S_1,s_1)\to(V,s)$, finite $\pi:W\to Y$, and smooth $h:Y\to S_1$ of relative dimension $n$, with geometrically integral fibres. Put $y=\pi(w)$ and $r=h\pi$; then $h(y)=s_1$, $ar=pjb$, $\pi^{-1}(y)=\{w\}$, and $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s_1)$ is purely transcendental. Its local-dimension parameter equals $n$ by step 1.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, scheme-level local structure applied to the supporting scheme.

proof.text: Apply pointed ambient etale lifting with ambient map $p:U\to V$, closed immersion $j$, base map $a$, and $(b,r,w)$. The compatibility $ar=pjb$ and both residue-field hypotheses were obtained in step 2. Obtain affine $X_1$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow X_1$, and an elementary etale $g_1:(X_1,i(w))\to(U,x)$ with $W=Z\times_U X_1$. Its structure map $f_1:X_1\to S_1$ satisfies $pg_1=af_1$ and $f_1i=h\pi$.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, compatible ambient lifting and its pointed diagram.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal G=b^*\mathcal H$. Pullback preserves finite type and quasi-coherence. Apply affine pushforward base change to $j:Z\to U$ (affine, as every closed immersion is by the definition of closed immersion) and the cartesian square of step 3: $i_*\mathcal G\cong g_1^*j_*\mathcal H\cong g_1^*u^*\mathcal F\cong(ug_1)^*\mathcal F$. The last isomorphism is pullback composition.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, final diagram, module identification via coherent.tex Tag 02KG.

proof.text: Take $X\prime=X_1$, $Z\prime=W$, $Y\prime=Y$, $S\prime=S_1$, $x\prime=i(w)$, $z\prime=w$, $y\prime=y$, $s\prime=s_1$, $g=ug_1$ and $e=va$. Etale composition makes $g,e$ etale. Their residue-field maps are composites of the isomorphisms in steps 1--3. Also $fg=vpg_1=vaf_1=ef_1$, and $f_1i=h\pi$. The four schemes are affine; the finite-presentation immersion is from step 3; the module isomorphism is step 4. All properties of $\pi,h,y,w$ from step 2 persist, since these maps and points are unchanged.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, composition with the initial open neighbourhoods and final assembly.
